title: Minang Geopark Run 2026 Review: Racing Past Sumatra's Iconic Clock Tower
seo_title: Minang Geopark Run 2026 Review | Bukittinggi, Sumatra
meta_description: Minang Geopark Run 2026 review: November 1 near Jam Gadang and Ngarai Sianok canyon -- the second leg of the Geopark Run Series in West Sumatra.
dek: Set for 1 November 2026 around Jam Gadang and the Ngarai Sianok canyon in Bukittinggi, this is the second leg of the Geopark Run Series, following the Ijen Geopark Run's debut earlier in the calendar.
verdict: The Minang Geopark Run puts runners next to two of West Sumatra's most iconic landmarks: Jam Gadang, a 26-metre clock tower built in 1926 as a gift from Queen Wilhelmina, and Ngarai Sianok, a roughly 100-metre deep, 15-kilometre-long canyon home to rare rafflesia and medicinal plants. As the second leg of the Geopark Run Series (following the Ijen Geopark Run covered elsewhere in this research), it carries the series' established branding into a completely different, canyon-and-colonial-landmark landscape. Three distances (5K/10K/21.1K) with open registration make this an accessible pick for runners who want genuinely dramatic Sumatran scenery.

sections.heading: The Series' Second Leg
paragraphs: Minang Geopark Run offers 5K, 10K and 21.1K distances around the Jam Gadang / Ngarai Sianok area of Bukittinggi, West Sumatra. [1] It's the second leg of the Geopark Run Series, following the inaugural Ijen Geopark Run covered elsewhere in this research batch -- giving this event the benefit of a proven organisational template even though Bukittinggi's landscape is entirely different from Ijen's volcanic highlands.

sections.heading: Racing Past a Colonial-Era Clock Tower
paragraphs: Jam Gadang -- Minangkabau for 'Big Clock' -- is a 26-metre clock tower and Bukittinggi's most recognisable landmark, built in 1926 during the Dutch colonial era as a gift from Queen Wilhelmina to the city's controleur. [2] Running past a structure this historically loaded gives the course genuine local character beyond a generic city-street race.

sections.heading: Alongside a Dramatic Canyon
paragraphs: Ngarai Sianok is a steep valley roughly 100 metres deep and 15 kilometres long, running from south of Koto Gadang to Sianok Anam Suku village. [3] The canyon is home to rare rafflesia and medicinal plants along its edges, and can be navigated by canoe or kayak via the Batang Sianok river running through it -- a genuinely dramatic natural backdrop for a road race.

sections.heading: A Young Series With Real Ambition
paragraphs: As only the second leg of a multi-year Geopark Run Series, there's limited independent track record yet, similar to the situation with the Ijen leg covered elsewhere in this research. [1] But the series' consistent branding and organisational approach across genuinely different Indonesian landscapes (volcanic highlands, then canyon country) suggests real ambition to establish a recognisable regional race brand.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a race through some of West Sumatra's most photogenic landmarks -- a colonial clock tower and a dramatic canyon -- the Minang Geopark Run on 1 November 2026 is a genuinely scenic pick. Registration is open now across all three distances.

faqs.question: When and where is the Minang Geopark Run 2026?
faqs.answer: 1 November 2026, around the Jam Gadang / Ngarai Sianok area of Bukittinggi, West Sumatra. Three distances are offered: 5K, 10K and 21.1K. Registration is currently open through the official Geopark Run Series website. [1]

faqs.question: What is Jam Gadang?
faqs.answer: A 26-metre clock tower and Bukittinggi's most iconic landmark, built in 1926 during the Dutch colonial era as a gift from Queen Wilhelmina. The race route passes near this and the Ngarai Sianok canyon. [2]

faqs.question: Is this related to the Ijen Geopark Run?
faqs.answer: Yes -- Minang Geopark Run is the second leg of the same Geopark Run Series that launched with the Ijen Geopark Run, carrying the series' branding into a completely different Sumatran canyon landscape. [1]
